identity.title: ALMA Reveals a Misaligned Inner Gas Disk inside the Large Cavity of a Transitional Disk

paper_type_evidence.quote: In this paper, we report a new high-resolution ALMA observation of both dust and gas in the J1604-2130 system.

evidence.quote: Recent GAIA DR2 reported that J1604-2130 is located at a distance of 150 pc.
Recent GAIA DR2 reported that J1604-2130 is located at a distance of 150 pc.

question.value: Are the two shadows seen in scattered light cast by an inner disk highly misaligned with the outer disk, as tested via mm surface brightness dips and a twisted butterfly pattern in gas moment 1 maps?

evidence.quote: Our goal is to test the hypothesis that the two shadows seen in scattered light imaging are cast by an inner disk highly misaligned with the outer disk
J1604-2130 was observed in ALMA cycle 3 program 2015.1.000888.S (PI: E. Akiyama) in Band 7.
J1604-2130 was observed in ALMA cycle 3 program 2015.1.000888.S (PI: E. Akiyama) in Band 7.

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: CO(3-2) window 234.375 MHz at 345.8 GHz; HCO+(4-3) window 468.750 MHz at 356.7 GHz; continuum 2 GHz windows at 344.0 and 355.5 GHz

evidence.quote: The other windows with bandwidth of 2.00 GHz were configured to obtain the continuum emission centered at 344.0 GHz and 355.5 GHz (channel widths of 15.625 MHz).
One spectral window with bandwidth of 234.375 MHz was centered at 345.8 GHz for the CO (3-2)
Another spectral window with bandwidth of 468.750 MHz was centered at 356.7 GHz for the HCO$^{+}$ (4-3)
The observations were conducted with the extended and compact configurations.

baselines.value: extended 15.1 m-1.1 km; compact 15.3 m-460.0 m

evidence.quote: The extended configuration array provided a maximum and minimum baseline length of 1.1 km and 15.1 m, respectively.
using ALMA observations with $\sim0$$''$2 angular resolution
The total integration time on source for target J1604-2130 was 62.8 minutes with extended configuration and 31.4 minutes with compact configuration.
The observation with the compact configuration was performed on March 10, 2016 with 37 operative antennas
J1604-2130 was observed in ALMA cycle 3 program 2015.1.000888.S (PI: E. Akiyama) in Band 7.
For the stellar position, we used the GAIA DR2.

findings_qualitative.value: Twisted butterfly moment 1 pattern in CO(3-2) indicates misaligned inner and outer disks; dips seen in continuum and gas.

evidence.quote: A twisted butterfly pattern is found in the moment 1 map of CO (3-2) emission line towards the center
